name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
description: Nintendo's 16-bit successor to the NES, sold in Japan as the Super Famicom. Its layered backgrounds, Mode 7 rotation and scaling, and Sony-designed sample-based sound made it home to Super Mario World, A Link to the Past, Super Metroid and a deep run of Japanese RPGs.

specs.graphics: S-PPU1 / S-PPU2, up to 256 of 32,768 colours, Mode 7
specs.sound: Sony SPC700 + S-DSP, 8 ADPCM channels, 64 KB audio RAM

curiosities: The sound chip was designed by Ken Kutaragi of Sony, who later led development of the PlayStation.
A Sony-built CD-ROM add-on, the 'Nintendo PlayStation', was announced in 1991 and then abandoned, leading Sony to make its own console.
Star Fox carried a Super FX coprocessor in its cartridge to draw real-time 3D polygons.
The North American model has a boxy grey-and-purple shell, while the Japanese and European versions share the rounded Super Famicom design.
